text: I'm getting duplicate rows when merging my orders and customers dataframes. Orders is 120k rows, customers is 9k. I'm using a left merge on customer_id. Merged ends up with 127,845 rows. I was expecting 120k, one customer per order. But clearly some orders repeat. E.g. order 12345 shows up twice. So I checked unique counts. Orders has 9000 unique customer_ids, customers has 8750. That explains it. Not every customer_id in orders is in customers, but that just makes some left merges become nulls. But the issue here is that the customers table is not unique on customer_id. If I check nunique on customer_id it's 8750, less than the 9000 rows, which means there are duplicate customer_ids. It's a data quality problem. That's what causes the expansion, and that's why I get 127k instead of 120k. So my next step is to dedupe the customers table. Either use drop_duplicates or drop_duplicates on customer_id. And then remeasure the result.
